```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

def task_func(df):
    step = 24 * 60 * 60  # constant 24-hour step in seconds
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()

    def _fallback(title):
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.set_xlabel("Date")
        ax.set_ylabel("Close Price")
        return [np.nan] * 7, ax

    if df is None:
        return _fallback("No data available")

    if not isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame):
        df = pd.DataFrame(df)

    if df.empty:
        return _fallback("No data available")

    data = df.copy()

    # --- Detect closing price column ---
    lower_map = {str(col).strip().lower(): col for col in data.columns}
    close_col = None

    for key in ("close", "closing price", "adj close", "adj_close", "adjclose"):
        if key in lower_map:
            close_col = lower_map[key]
            break

    if close_col is None:
        for col in reversed(list(data.columns)):
            if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[col]):
                close_col = col
                break

    if close_col is None:
        close_col = data.columns[-1]

    close_series = pd.to_numeric(data[close_col], errors="coerce")

    # --- Detect time information ---
    time_series = None

    if isinstance(data.index, pd.DatetimeIndex):
        time_series = pd.Series(data.index, index=data.index)
    else:
        datetime_candidates = []
        for col in data.columns:
            if col == close_col:
                continue
            name = str(col).strip().lower()
            if any(k in name for k in ("date", "datetime", "timestamp", "time")):
                datetime_candidates.append(col)

        # Prefer obvious date/time columns and only accept columns that parse well as datetimes.
        for col in datetime_candidates:
            s = data[col]
            if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(s):
                time_series = pd.Series(pd.to_datetime(s, errors="coerce"), index=data.index)
                break
            if pd.api.types.is_object_dtype(s) or pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(s):
                parsed = pd.to_datetime(s, errors="coerce")
                required = 1 if len(s) == 1 else max(2, (len(s) + 1) // 2)
                if parsed.notna().sum() >= required:
                    time_series = pd.Series(parsed, index=data.index)
                    break

        if time_series is None and not isinstance(data.index, pd.RangeIndex):
            parsed_index = pd.to_datetime(data.index, errors="coerce")
            required = 1 if len(data.index) == 1 else max(2, (len(data.index) + 1) // 2)
            if pd.Series(parsed_index).notna().sum() >= required:
                time_series = pd.Series(parsed_index, index=data.index)

    # Fallback to synthetic timestamps if no usable time source exists.
    if time_series is None:
        time_seconds = pd.Series(np.arange(len(data), dtype=float) * step, index=data.index)
    else:
        if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(time_series):
            ts = pd.to_datetime(time_series, errors="coerce")
            if getattr(ts.dt, "tz", None) is not None:
                ts = ts.dt.tz_convert(None)
            time_seconds = pd.Series(ts.astype("int64") // 10**9, index=data.index)
        else:
            time_seconds = pd.to_numeric(time_series, errors="coerce")

    work = pd.DataFrame({"time": time_seconds, "close": close_series}).dropna()

    if work.empty:
        return _fallback("Insufficient data for regression")

    work = work.sort_values("time")
    work = work.groupby("time", as_index=False)["close"].mean()

    # If there is not enough variation in time to fit a regression, repeat the last price.
    if len(work) < 2 or work["time"].nunique() < 2:
        last_price = float(work["close"].iloc[-1])
        preds = [last_price] * 7
        future_times = work["time"].iloc[-1] + step * np.arange(1, 8)

        hist_x = pd.to_datetime(work["time"], unit="s", errors="coerce")
        future_x = pd.to_datetime(future_times, unit="s", errors="coerce")

        ax.plot(hist_x, work["close"], label="Historical Close", color="tab:blue")
        ax.plot(future_x, preds, "--o", label="Predicted Close", color="tab:orange")
        ax.axvline(hist_x.iloc[-1], color="gray", linestyle=":", alpha=0.7)
        ax.set_title("Stock Closing Price Forecast")
        ax.set_xlabel("Date")
        ax.set_ylabel("Close Price")
        ax.legend()
        fig.autofmt_xdate()
        return preds, ax

    # --- Fit simple linear regression on time (seconds) vs close price ---
    base_time = float(work["time"].iloc[0])
    X = (work["time"].to_numpy(dtype=float) - base_time).reshape(-1, 1)
    y = work["close"].to_numpy(dtype=float)

    model = LinearRegression()
    model.fit(X, y)

    # --- Predict the next 7 days using a fixed 24*60*60 second step ---
    future_times = work["time"].iloc[-1] + step * np.arange(1, 8, dtype=float)
    future_X = (future_times - base_time).reshape(-1, 1)
    preds = model.predict(future_X).astype(float).tolist()

    # --- Plot historical and predicted data ---
    hist_x = pd.to_datetime(work["time"], unit="s", errors="coerce")
    future_x = pd.to_datetime(future_times, unit="s", errors="coerce")

    ax.plot(hist_x, work["close"], label="Historical Close", color="tab:blue")
    ax.plot(future_x, preds, "--o", label="Predicted Close", color="tab:orange")
    ax.axvline(hist_x.iloc[-1], color="gray", linestyle=":", alpha=0.7)
    ax.set_title("Stock Closing Price Forecast")
    ax.set_xlabel("Date")
    ax.set_ylabel("Close Price")
    ax.legend()
    fig.autofmt_xdate()

    return preds, ax
```
